newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 29.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 29.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Brand-name Products, Consumer Trends, Media and the Internet.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - Luxury car maker Mercedes-Benz AG will roll out its new A-class compact car on Tuesday, a bid to lure customers at a younger age into the Mercedes brand and to help expand the car maker's sales to one million vehicles by the turn of the century. (Reuter)
BONN - German magazines lost further advertising income to television in 1996, continuing a decade-long trend, the Association of German Periodical Publishers says. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - The Frankfurt "Marketing Services" convention that closed on Saturday had about 20,000 visitors, says the convention centre where it was held. Direct and event marketing and media services attracted particular attention during the six-day event. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Embattled digital television station DF1, owned by Munich media investor Leo Kirch, says it is considering a new communications strategy. It has solicited new concepts from other media agencies, but says Munich-based ServicePlan will continue to represent it. (Horizont/Reuters)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MUNICH - Software giant Microsoft Corp says it plans to hold a news conference on May 20 for an announcement related to Windows NT and a large German information technology company. The company has declined to give further details. (Reuter)

BONN - Interior minister Manfred Kanther has called for increased efforts to fight crime on the Internet and demanded that cyber-sheriffs have keys to unlock coded messages. Kanther says the government does not want to stifle development of the Internet through excessive regulation, particularly in the area of encryption, which protects data from unwanted access. (Reuter)
ZURICH - TA-Media AG, the second largest Swiss publishing group after Ringier, expects another difficult year in 1997 and plans to implement cuts. (Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
FRIEDRICHSHAFEN - The aerospace unit of industrial group Daimler-Benz AG says it is interested in buying the defence electronics business of Siemens AG. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Ferdinand Piech, the head of the carmaker Volkswagen AG says he plans to more than quadruple the group's pre-tax profit by the end of the century. (Reuter)
STUTTGART - Daimler-Benz Ag denies comments made at the weekend from a top union leader that the company planned to cut about 23,000 jobs in the coming years. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Banking group Deutsche Bank AG says it is providing more start-up money for innovative technology firms, but warns that big reforms are needed to ensure an adequate flow of venture capital in Germany. (Reuter)
DUESSELDORF - Chemical group Henkel KGaA says it is looking abroad for future growth after a positive start to its 1997 business year. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
MUNICH - Susanne Lang is taking over as programming public relations representative at the Munich-based private television channel Pro Sieben. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Max magazine publisher Dirk Manthey is stepping down as editor-in-chief, making room for Uwe Killing. (Horizont)
Deborah Cole, Berlin Newsroom, 49-30-20398114
